Title: Selangor seeks legal advice on assemblyman's status, possible by-election
Article:
news@nst.com.my
KUALA PILAH: The Selangor government is reviewing claims that a state assemblyman has lost his eligibility to remain in office.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state government had received preliminary information on the matter and was seeking legal advice before deciding on further action, including whether a by-election would be required.
He said the issue was expected to be raised during the state assembly sitting scheduled for Oct 3.
"We have received some preliminary information on the matter.
"I am currently reviewing it with our legal advisers, and it is possible that the Speaker will inform the House about it during the sitting.
"We need to verify the allegation, particularly the claim regarding the disqualification or loss of eligibility of a Selangor state assembly member," he said.
He said this when met after the Kuala Pilah Berselawat and Munajat Perdana programme at Dataran Melang last night.
Amirudin said that if the review found there was a legal requirement to hold a by-election, the matter would be referred to the Election Commission.
However, he declined to identify the assemblyman involved or provide details of the allegation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: 28-time blood donor inspires Malaysians with message
Article:
​​
KUALA LUMPUR: A blood donor has captured public attention after sharing how his regular donations helped save the life of a child battling thalassaemia.
Known only as Vince, the man shared on Threads that he had donated blood 28 times, with each donation involving 450ml of blood.
He said he had been contacted several times by Seberang Jaya Hospital to donate, and later learnt that his blood type matched that of a child receiving treatment for thalassaemia.
"I asked why the hospital always contacted me. The doctor replied, 'because your blood matches the blood of a Malay child with thalassaemia'," he said.
Vince, who has AB+ RH+ blood type, said blood donation was ultimately about saving lives and should not be viewed through the lens of race or background.
"My blood has never known Malay, Chinese or Indian. It is only meant to save lives. We help each other when needed. I am a Malaysian."
His post received nearly 60,000 likes and thousands of shares, with many Malaysians praising his contribution and message of compassion.
The Health Ministry also responded to the post, expressing appreciation to Vince and all blood donors who continue to come forward regardless of differences.
The ministry said the story served as a reminder that blood does not recognise race, religion or background, but only its purpose of saving lives.
"Every drop of blood becomes hope and a lifeline for someone in need, and in this case, a child.
"That is compassion, a symbol of kindness without boundaries," it said.
The post also prompted other donors and recipients to share their own experiences.
One user said he had donated blood 101 times and had never known who received his blood, adding that his responsibility was simply to help those in need.
"This is my 101st time. I have never known who received my blood. What matters is that I have completed my duty. See you on Sept 12 for my 102nd donation," he wrote.
Another user thanked blood donors, saying her child had received several blood transfusions as part of ongoing treatment.
"Thank you to all the kind and amazing donors. My special child has received your kindness several times. May you be blessed with good health and prosperity."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH confident of keeping Negri Sembilan with 22-seat target
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Pakatan Harapan is confident of retaining power in Negri Sembilan, with a target of winning between 21 and 22 of the 36 seats up for grabs in the state election.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the target was achievable based on voters' ability to evaluate PH's performance since 2018, as well as the two-term administration record of Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun.
"We will work hard to secure a minimum of 19 seats and, if we are capable of achieving more, we may win between 21 and 22 seats.
"That is our best estimate.
"However, we believe in the wisdom of voters and will continue campaigning consistently to ensure the mandate to form the state government is retained," he said.
He said this when met after the Kuala Pilah Berselawat and Negri Sembilan Perdana Munajat programme at Dataran Melang last night.
Amirudin, however, acknowledged that the political landscape in this state election would be more challenging due to changes in party alliances.
"2018 was PH's best year when we won 20 seats.
"Following the BN and PH alliance in 2023, we secured about 31 seats.
"This time, the challenge is slightly different as the election landscape and political alliances have also changed.
"We are aware of the challenges and are still working to secure a comfortable number of seats to form the government," he said.
On claims that the "blue wave" in Johor would also sweep through Negri Sembilan, Amirudin said it was merely a narrative being pushed by Barisan Nasional.
"Of course, this is something created by BN. However, here we have a track record of leadership and the strength of the Menteri Besar himself.
"We have faced and overcome the green wave in Selangor and Negri Sembilan.
"We view the current dynamics as something new and will continue to present solutions based on the Malaysia Madani concept and the unity of the people, instead of rhetoric that divides society along racial lines," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iranian army says drones target key US facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base
Article:
MANAMA, (Bahrain): Iran's army said Thursday it targeted key US military facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base with one-way attack drones amid an exchange of attacks between Teheran and Washington across the West Asia region, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
In a statement, the army's public relations office said the operation was carried out in retaliation for the killing of an Iranian Air Force Su-24 pilot at the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran in February, the official IRNA news agency reported.
It said the drones struck power generators, navigation systems and administrative and support buildings used by what it described as the US military at Sheikh Isa Air Base.
The military claimed that repeated attacks on US bases in the region over recent days had inflicted "significant damage" on military equipment and facilities despite the bases being protected by multiple air defence systems.
It described Sheikh Isa Air Base as one of the most important US military installations in the Gulf region, saying it hosts reconnaissance aircraft and serves as a major maintenance centre for helicopters and drone components.
The statement claimed the repeated attacks by Iran's armed forces had caused serious damage to the base's combat and logistical support capabilities.
There was no immediate comment from Bahraini or US authorities on the claim. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BOJ to keep rates steady, deliver hawkish signal as government props up yen
Article:
TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but signal its resolve to continue pushing up borrowing costs, after the government intervened to boost the weak yen, keeping pressure on the central bank to show its hawkishness.
Japan conducted yen-buying, dollar-selling market intervention in New York markets on Thursday, a market source said, pulling the sagging currency from four-decade lows, hours before the BOJ concludes a two-day policy meeting.
Having just raised rates in June, the BOJ is widely expected to keep short-term interest rates steady at one per cent.
Hawkish board member Hajime Takata may dissent and propose a hike to 1.25 per cent, some analysts say.
The BOJ meeting follows that of the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday, at which the board kept interest rates steady but with three dissenters calling for a quarter-percentage-point hike.
Markets are focusing on the BOJ's quarterly outlook report and Governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting news briefing for clues on how soon it could raise still-low borrowing costs.
In the report, the board is seen revising up its growth forecast for fiscal 2026 on receding fears of a severe hit from the Middle East conflict, sources have told Reuters.
The board is also likely to cut its inflation forecast due to the effect of subsidies and a drop in oil costs from levels seen in April, they said, though jittery oil markets and rising import costs from a weak yen may keep any downgrade small.
"Although inflation forecasts may be revised lower, stronger growth would reinforce confidence that the economy can withstand further policy normalisation," said Kei Fujimoto, senior economist at SuMi Trust.
"My baseline scenario remains that the BOJ raises rates roughly once every six months. However, given the improving growth backdrop, together with accelerating import-price inflation, the possibility of a faster pace of tightening cannot be ruled out," he said.
WEAK-YEN RISK
The BOJ raised rates to a 31-year high in June and signalled its readiness to tighten further as it focuses on taming price pressures from the energy shock.
Most analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise rates again to 1.25 per cent by year-end.
The slow pace of rate hikes has been blamed for pushing the yen to a 40-year low, leading to rising import costs that hurt households and retailers.
Ueda will face the challenge of talking down the yen bears through hawkish communication, particularly with looming prospects of US rate hikes weighing on the yen's value against the dollar, analysts say.
But pressure from a dovish administration and the potential economic hit from a 7.1-magnitude earthquake in the southern prefecture of Kumamoto, home to plants of major manufacturers and chipmakers, may dampen the hawkish mood, some analysts say.
So far, the economy appears to have weathered the hit from rising fuel costs and supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict, which are driving up inflation.
Factory output rose in June and manufacturers projected further increases this month and next, data showed on Friday.
Separate data also showed annual core inflation in Japan's capital accelerated to 1.70 per cent in July, a sign of broadening price pressures from the Middle East conflict.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea conducts rare dollar-selling intervention, source says
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea's foreign exchange authorities conducted a rare dollar-selling intervention on Thursday, sending the won to a nine-month high, a market source told Reuters on Friday.
Seoul's move came alongside Japan's yen-buying, dollar-selling market intervention in New York markets on Thursday, pulling the yen from four-decade lows.
"Foreign exchange officials conducted rare dollar-selling intervention overnight," the source said, declining to be identified.
The won on Thursday strengthened two per cent to its strongest level since Oct 20 at 1,418.0 per US dollar.
The currency, which hit a 17-year low of 1,561.50 last month, has gained more than eight per cent this month, putting it on track for its biggest monthly jump since March 2009.
A foreign exchange official at the finance ministry declined to confirm the intervention.
It is suspected that South Korea and Japan intervened together, since the countries said they would coordinate closely, a South Korean currency trader said.
On July 2, South Korea's vice finance chief said at a press conference that Seoul was closely communicating with Japan and other key allies on foreign exchange issues.
Japan's top currency diplomat followed those comments on July 7, saying Tokyo was closely communicating with Seoul's foreign exchange officials as the financial markets of Japan and South Korea sometimes exhibit similar movements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI spending boom could be market's biggest risk: Franklin Income CIO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The capital expenditure (capex) needed around artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure could be a key risk in markets going into the second half of the year.
Franklin Income Investors chief investment officer Ed Perks said data centre and large infrastructure projects are drawing on similar resources and competing for capital at the same time.
This creates the potential for bottlenecks as companies pursue massive buildouts, Perks said.
"The key questions are where capex goes from here, when it peaks and how much financing the market will need to absorb.
"Material delays in AI infrastructure projects, or a slowdown in spending plans, could create volatility risk for markets," he said in a report.
He said these investment plans may have important implications beyond the current cycle, which is why it is important to assess the risks before they become more visible in market pricing.
He said the uncertain market environment reinforces the importance of maintaining a long-term perspective.
"As companies seek significant financing for AI infrastructure and other large-scale projects, we believe providers of capital can remain patient.
"The competition for capital may create opportunities, but discipline will be important as investors evaluate the durability of cash flows, the timing of returns and the risks tied to execution," said Perks.
He said it is important for investors to stay nimble with asset allocation and diversified across sectors remains, particularly in an environment shaped by policy uncertainty, range-bound rates, AI-related investment and periodic market dislocations.
Perks said the US-Iran conflict defined the first half of 2026 as a war in the Middle East erupted, driving an energy shock, reigniting inflationary pressures and forcing central banks globally into a hawkish pivot.
This event shaped the macro backdrop for all asset classes.
"Markets at times have shifted from expectations for rate cuts to concerns that policy may remain restrictive for longer.
"Some of these swings reflected short-term market reactions rather than durable changes in the economic outlook."

Title: Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 begins today
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) has returned to Sarawak, with the three-day Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak Segulai Sejalai 2026 beginning today and running until Sunday at the Kota Samarahan Municipal Council grounds.
Now in its 23rd year, KJH, recognised by The Malaysia Book of Records as the Longest Running Outdoor Carnival, continues to champion family and community values through a wide range of entertainment, recreational, health and lifestyle activities catering to people of all ages.
Organised by Media Prima Bhd in strategic collaboration with the Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry (MTCP), the carnival also provides visitors with the opportunity to engage with various agencies under the ministry through exhibitions, activities and initiatives held throughout the event.
Several activities have been lined up over the three-day carnival, including the Drama Sangat Karaoke Competition, the Buletin Challenge, meet and greet sessions with TV3 drama cast members and TV9 personalities, a children's colouring contest, free health and dental screenings, the Zumba Challenge and Jom Lokal Jam.
Adding to the excitement are Media Prima personalities, including Shafiq Adnan, Afrina Romzi, Saree Abdullah, Fahiz Ariff, Haniff of Hot FM and Kieran of KoolFM, who will take part in interactive segments and meet visitors throughout the carnival.
The highlight of the event is the Jom Heboh Concert, which will be held on Saturday and Sunday nights.
Tomorrow night's concert will feature performances by Haiza Hanafi, Mariam Saim, Aepul Roza, Fiq Halim, Aweera and Kristal X, while the second night will showcase Baby Shima, Wany Hasrita, K.O.I, Syamel and Marsha Milan, along with several other artistes, bringing this year's edition to a close.
Following the encouraging response to its inaugural edition last year, the Jom Heboh Fun Run returns for a second year, promising participants an even more exciting experience.
For the first time, participants will receive an exclusive finisher's medal, in addition to the official event jersey, race bib, tote bag and commemorative merchandise.
This year, the run has been expanded to include two categories: 5km and 8km.
To encourage greater family participation, organisers have also introduced a Family Package for the 5km category, offering a special registration rate for four participants under a single entry.
Participants will also stand a chance to win lucky draw prizes while enjoying the event alongside Media Prima personalities and guest artistes, including Aepul Roza, Fiq Halim and Aweera.
In addition to the Media Prima booth, visitors can explore booths by various agencies under MTCP, entrepreneurs mentored by the Sarawak International Trade, Industry and Investment Ministry, as well as participating companies and brands throughout the carnival.
Among the participating brands are Grab, which is offering e-hailing discount codes, the Employees Provident Fund, GPR Cookies, Ayam Dindings, Pawada, CelcomDigi, Weststar Maxus and several other local and international brands.
Visitors can also enjoy a wide selection of popular food while taking part in interactive activities at the various booths.
For more information, visit the official Jom Heboh website at www.jomheboh.com.my or follow Jom Heboh's official social media platforms.

Title: Gold rises on weaker US dollar, soft inflation data
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold rose on Thursday as the US dollar weakened and inflation eased, with traders dialling back bets on interest rate hikes a day after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh offered little clarity on policy.
Spot gold was up one per cent at US$4,104.59 per ounce by 1:40 p.m. EDT (1740 GMT).
US gold futures for August delivery gained 1.60 per cent to settle at US$4,160.60.
The dollar fell 0.80 per cent as the yen strengthened, while traders remained on alert for possible intervention by Japanese authorities to prop up the battered currency.
A weaker dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more affordable for buyers overseas.
Prices were little changed after a Commerce Department report showed the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index fell 0.10 per cent in June, in line with economists' expectations in a Reuters poll.
The easing is likely to be temporary as renewed hostilities in the Middle East raise oil prices.
The PCE data looks "a little bit better than the market expected. So for now the environment on the inflation side is more or less stable," said Bart Melek, global head of commodity strategy at TD Securities.
"The Middle East war isn't looking like it's getting over anytime soon. So these inflation pressures that were reversed over the last few months may come back.
"And the view out there is that the central bank will ultimately respond. And that is keeping gold breaking out beyond the resistance levels, which we see at about 4150, 4200."
The Fed on Wednesday left interest rates unchanged.
After the release of the policy statement, Warsh pledged an unwavering commitment to bring inflation down, a message that left markets confused about just what he was prepared to do.
Spot gold prices rose about two per cent after the policy decision.
Traders see a 61 per cent chance of a rate hike at the Fed's Sept 15-16 meeting, down from about 77 per cent before the Fed meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.
Higher-for-longer rates tend to diminish bullion's appeal due to its non-yielding characteristic.
US jobless claims increased less than expected last week, suggesting labour market conditions remained stable, another government report showed.
Spot silver rose two per cent to US$58.79 per ounce, platinum gained 2.50 per cent to US$1,652.32, and palladium climbed 4.40 per cent to US$1,301.39.

Title: Oil settles down on proposed Saudi-led maritime defence coalition
Article:
NEW YORK: Oil prices settled lower on Thursday after a volatile session, as traders digested proposed plans for a Saudi Arabia-led maritime coalition to boost defence cooperation around the Red Sea.
Saudi Arabia seeks to lead a coalition to boost defence cooperation in the Bab El-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
The Saudi defence ministry said 14 states, including Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan and Djibouti, have issued a joint statement in support of the proposed multinational maritime defence coalition.
Brent futures settled down US$1.71, or 1.88 per cent, at US$89.03 a barrel.
Trade was choppy and Brent touched a session high of US$93.31 after Washington and Tehran traded strikes on each other's military targets again.
US West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled down 87 cents, or 1.03 per cent, at US$83.59, after hitting a high of US$85.94.
Iran-aligned Houthi militants in Yemen declared a naval blockade last week on Saudi Arabia, threatening the Red Sea route for its oil exports, an alternative to the largely blockaded Strait of Hormuz.
"There is this sense that there is a lot of supply waiting to hit market once all of this is resolved, and that is a weight against any kind of dramatic price rise," said John Kilduff, partner at Again Capital.
Iran and Oman continued talks on the management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Iranian Labour News Agency.
On Wednesday, a senior Iranian official said Iran had ruled out Oman's proposal for regional joint management of the waterway.
"The fact that Oman is in talks with Iran could suggest that progress is being made on re-opening the Strait of Hormuz," said Hamad Hussain, senior climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics.
The strait, which normally handles around a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows, has remained a focal point for oil markets since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran on Feb 28.
"Until safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz is no longer a gamble, the risk premium in oil is not going anywhere — hope for diplomacy is welcome, but the market is pricing in the reality of ongoing strikes," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT WIDENS
The US military said it had hit dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran in an operation launched after Tehran fired ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East.
No US aircraft were destroyed or damaged in the recent attempted Iranian attacks, the US military said on Thursday, denying a claim it said was made by Iran's Revolutionary Guards that three US F-35 jets and three other aircraft were destroyed.
"That lowers temperature on the situation," said Again Capital's Kilduff.
A drone caused a fire that engulfed two gas vessels at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta, the Egyptian cabinet said on Thursday, confirming that the blaze which erupted a day earlier was the result of an attack rather than an accident.
Egypt has secured alternative sources to cover its energy demands after the attack, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said later on Thursday.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia this week from Iraqi territory in coordination with Iraqi armed groups, according to assessments by Saudi Arabia and regional partners, reflecting growing coordination among Iran-aligned militias, two officials in the region said.
The attacks included strikes on oil facilities in Saudi Arabia's eastern province, the kingdom's main crude hub.
In another blow to supply, tankers planned for loading at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) terminal are heading away from the Black Sea after a vessel was hit during loading at the terminal on Thursday, two sources said, and shipping data showed.
A Ukrainian drone attack caused a fire at Lukoil's Perm refinery that damaged and forced the shutdown of one of its crude distillation units, two industry sources told Reuters.
"Given the disruption to flows through several maritime chokepoints, as well as the rapid depletion of oil inventories, prices could feasibly be even higher than where they sit currently," Capital Economics' Hussain added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH RCI a lesson in governance failure, voters told
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Governance and integrity should be the key considerations for voters in the 16th Negri Sembilan election to prevent further erosion of the nation's institutions through corruption and abuse of power, says Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Referring to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), he said its findings should serve as a reminder of the consequences of weak governance and abuse of power.
He said although the report submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong did not use colloquial terms such as "sakau'' (to loot or embezzle), it clearly pointed to corruption and misappropriation.
"Of course, the RCI report presented to His Majesty does not use the word 'sakau' because it is an official document, but it clearly reveals that corrupt practices took place.
"The commission's findings have been referred to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) for further action," he said at a PH ceramah in the Senaling state constituency tonight.
Also present was PH's Senaling candidate Mohd Hanis Alimin, who will face Barisan Nasional's Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil and Bersatu's Mohd Izaffi Istear Khan in a three-cornered contest.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said publication of the RCI report had previously been deferred to allow time for TH's restructuring and financial recovery.
He said this was necessary to avoid triggering panic or a loss of confidence among depositors that could have led to large-scale withdrawals.
He urged voters to choose leaders with integrity to safeguard the country's future.
"Choose the wrong leaders and you risk damaging our assets, our state and our country. Choose candidates who are sincere, hardworking and have integrity to represent the people," he said.
Polling for the Negri Sembilan election will take place tomorrow, with 867,151 registered voters casting their ballots to elect representatives for 36 state seats. A total of 103 candidates are contesting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji's buyback of Urusharta Jamaah assets based on commercial value, not obligation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji says its recent repurchase of selected assets from Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd reflects a disciplined investment strategy and should not be viewed as a reversal of its 2018 restructuring programme.
Under the restructuring exercise, Urusharta Jamaah - a government-owned special purpose vehicle - bought underperforming and problematic Tabung Haji assets to help eliminate a financial deficit that had exceeded RM10 billion.
Under the restructuring, assets with a carrying value of RM9.7 billion were sold to Urusharta for RM19.9 billion.
Urusharta Jamaah financed the acquisition by issuing two series of sukuk, backed by government letters of support.
As part of the arrangement, Tabung Haji was granted a "Right of First Refusal" over those assets should Urusharta Jamaah decide to sell them in the future.
Tabung Haji emphasised that this right gave it priority to consider any acquisition but did not oblige it to buy back any asset.
Throughout the life of the sukuk issued to finance the restructuring, Urusharta Jamaah
made several offers to Tabung Haji, all of which were declined because they did not satisfy the institution's investment and commercial criteria.
Following a fresh assessment this year, Tabung Haji bought back the Tun Razak Exchange land for RM270 million, significantly below its original transfer price of RM400 million.
It also acquired UJ Estates (Holdings) Sdn Bhd's oil palm plantations for RM695 million, compared with the original transfer price of RM800 million.
Tabung Haji said the acquisitions were made only because the assets now offer value to its investment portfolio.
They are expected to strengthen long-term returns while protecting the interests of depositors, it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Microsoft sets record with near US$450bil single-day gain in market value
Article:
NEW YORK: Microsoft added nearly US$450 billion in market value on Thursday, the largest one-day gain on record for a company, after it forecast stronger-than-expected cloud growth and signalled continued cash generation through its new fiscal year.
The software giant's shares closed up more than 15 per cent, lifting its market capitalisation to US$3.35 trillion, surpassing chip giant Nvidia's previous record one-day gain of US$441 billion on April 9, 2025, according to LSEG data.
"Microsoft reported a very strong quarter and it struck the tone markets are looking to hear as the key drivers of growth came from the cloud and AI divisions," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management.
The results offered fresh evidence that Microsoft's massive AI investments are beginning to pay off, helping ease investor concerns that heavy spending on data centres and computing infrastructure could outpace demand.
Microsoft has lagged some of its "Magnificent Seven" peers this year, with its stock down more than 18 per cent up to Wednesday's close.
At least nine brokerages raised the target price on the stock, with the mean target now US$560.90.
Microsoft said its spending plans remain unchanged and that it expects capital expenditures of US$50 billion for the fiscal first quarter of 2027 and US$175 billion for the 2026 calendar year.
In its first quarter, Microsoft expects Azure to grow 45 per cent on a constant-currency basis, well above analysts' estimate of a 40.92 per cent increase, according to Visible Alpha data.
"The key question was whether it could shift the conversation from how much it is spending on AI to what it is earning from those investments, and the results suggested meaningful progress," Direxion's head of capital markets, Jake Behan, said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Why Tabung Haji's 2018 restructuring was unavoidable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji has defended its 2018 restructuring exercise, describing it as a necessary intervention to prevent insolvency and safeguard the savings of more than nine million depositors.
Tabung Haji, in a statement today, said concerns over its financial position had been building for several years.
Since 2014, Bank Negara Malaysia had warned that consistently high profit distributions were eroding the fund's already limited reserves.
This had eventually pushed the reserves into negative territory and exposed the institution to the risk of a large-scale depositor withdrawal.
The Auditor General's 2017 financial report also highlighted accounting practices that did not accurately reflect Tabung Haji's true financial position.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) later concluded that the audit should have classified the issue as non-compliance rather than issuing a clean audit opinion with only an "Emphasis of Matter".
By the end of 2018, the gap between Tabung Haji's assets and liabilities had widened to more than RM10 billion.
Tabung Haji said without urgent intervention it would not have met the requirements of the Tabung Haji Act to declare any profit distribution.
This would have potentially triggered a depositor run that could have forced distressed asset sales and created wider financial market instability.
Tabung Haji said the restructuring was therefore designed to restore solvency, protect depositors' funds and place the institution on a financially sustainable footing for the future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji completes financial turnaround, overcomes RM12.6bil in investment losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji says it has restored its financial strength following a comprehensive recovery and restructuring programme launched in 2018.
The recovery plan had addressed RM12.6 billion in investment losses, comprising RM10 billion through the 2018 restructuring and a further RM2.6 billion progressively until the end of 2025.
This had positioned it for long-term sustainability and improved returns for depositors, Tabung Haji said in a statement today.
According to the fund, the turnaround has been driven by strategic reforms, stronger corporate governance and prudent financial management under its current leadership.
The measures have enabled it to rebuild confidence among depositors while operating independently without further government intervention.
The improvement is reflected in its steadily rising profit distributions, it said.
Returns have increased from 1.25 per cent in 2018, the year the restructuring was implemented, to 3.25 per cent in 2024 and 3.50 per cent in 2025.
Tabung Haji stressed that the distributions were declared only after recognising impairment losses of RM2.6 billion on problematic assets that could not be transferred during the restructuring exercise.
This demonstrated a more transparent and prudent approach to financial reporting.
Tabung Haji said its financial position is now significantly stronger and that it has begun rebuilding reserves to support future growth and financial resilience.
The fund reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding depositors' savings, strengthening public confidence and ensuring it continues to operate with integrity, accountability and sound financial discipline.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: When trust is broken
Article:
TRUST is one of the most valuable assets in any workplace. It forms the foundation of strong working relationships, effective communication, and successful teamwork.
Once trust has been broken, however, rebuilding it is neither quick nor easy.
Betraying your boss, whether through dishonesty, disloyalty, broken confidentiality, or poor judgement, can damage not only your professional reputation but also the confidence others have in your character.
Although the road back is difficult, it is not impossible. Rebuilding trust requires genuine remorse, consistent action, patience, and a commitment to personal growth.
The first and most important step is accepting full responsibility for your actions. It is natural to feel embarrassed or defensive when confronted with a mistake, but attempting to justify your behaviour or shift blame will only deepen the damage.
A sincere acknowledgement of what happened demonstrates maturity and integrity. Owning your actions without excuses shows that you understand the seriousness of your betrayal and are prepared to face its consequences.
A genuine apology is essential. A meaningful apology goes beyond simply saying "I'm sorry."
It should recognise the impact your actions have had on your boss, your colleagues, and the wider workplace. It should also make it clear that you understand why trust has been damaged.
Most importantly, your apology should not be accompanied by conditions or expectations of immediate forgiveness.
Trust is earned, not demanded. Once you have apologised, your focus must shift from words to actions.
Promises alone have little value after trust has been broken. Your boss will naturally judge you by your behaviour rather than your intentions.
This means arriving on time, completing tasks diligently, meeting deadlines, and consistently demonstrating reliability. Every small action becomes an opportunity to prove that you are committed to changing.
Patience is another vital ingredient in rebuilding trust. Many people expect that a heartfelt apology should quickly restore relationships, but this is rarely the case.
Your boss may remain cautious, distant, or sceptical for some time. These reactions are understandable.
Respect their need for time and avoid becoming frustrated if trust does not return as quickly as you would like.
Healing professional relationships often takes far longer than damaging them.
Honesty must become a daily habit. If mistakes occur, admit them immediately rather than attempting to conceal them. Transparency demonstrates that you have learned from your previous behaviour.
Even when the truth is uncomfortable, it is always better than allowing another breach of trust to develop.
Small acts of honesty, repeated consistently, gradually rebuild confidence.
Consistency is often more powerful than dramatic gestures. Employees sometimes believe they must perform extraordinary acts to regain favour, but trust is usually rebuilt through ordinary behaviour carried out exceptionally well.
Completing routine responsibilities with care, communicating openly, and following through on commitments every day creates a pattern of dependability.
Over time, these repeated actions become evidence of genuine change.
Professionalism should also guide every interaction.
Avoid workplace gossip, negativity, or behaviour that could create further doubt about your character. Show respect to everyone, regardless of their position.
Your conduct should demonstrate that you have become someone who contributes positively to the workplace rather than creating unnecessary conflict or uncertainty.
It is equally important to understand why the betrayal occurred in the first place. Without honest self-reflection, there is a risk of repeating the same behaviour.
Ask yourself whether your actions were driven by fear, ambition, resentment, poor judgement, or external pressure.
Understanding the root cause allows you to address the underlying issue instead of merely treating the symptoms.
Personal growth begins with self-awareness. Seeking constructive feedback can also demonstrate humility.
Your boss may not always be willing to provide it immediately, but showing a willingness to learn sends a positive message.
Listen carefully without becoming defensive. Accept criticism as an opportunity to improve rather than as a personal attack.
People who actively seek improvement often regain respect more quickly than those who simply hope the past will be forgotten.
Rebuilding trust also requires emotional resilience. There may be uncomfortable conversations, reduced responsibilities, or missed opportunities while your boss assesses whether you can be relied upon again.
Rather than viewing these setbacks as punishment, see them as part of the rebuilding process. Respond with professionalism and determination instead of resentment.
Over time, your reputation can begin to recover. While people may never completely forget what happened, they can come to recognise that you have changed.
Many respected professionals have recovered from serious mistakes because they consistently demonstrated honesty, accountability, and reliability over an extended period.
Character is not defined solely by failure but by how one responds to it.
Ultimately, rebuilding trust after betraying your boss is less about convincing others and more about becoming a better professional. Genuine change cannot be rushed or performed for appearances.
It must be reflected in daily decisions, consistent behaviour, and unwavering integrity. Every interaction becomes an opportunity to reinforce your commitment to earning back confidence.
Trust is fragile, but it is not beyond repair. While rebuilding it requires humility, patience, and perseverance, it is possible for those who are willing to accept responsibility and demonstrate lasting change.
By replacing excuses with accountability, promises with consistent action, and self-interest with integrity, you can gradually restore confidence and rebuild a stronger, more respectful professional relationship than before.

Title: Wall Street ends sharply higher, lifted by soaring Microsoft
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street ended sharply higher on Thursday, with chip stocks jumping and Microsoft logging its biggest daily percentage gain in 18 years after the technology giant gave a stellar forecast that eased fears about massive spending on AI infrastructure.
Microsoft jumped over 15 per cent, boosting its stock market value by US$450 billion, the greatest-ever single-day increase for a company on Wall Street.
The tech heavyweight forecast quarterly sales and cloud growth above expectations. It also reported capital expenditures below estimates and said it expects to keep generating cash through its fiscal 2027, which has just begun.
This year, investors have been spooked by heavy spending on AI at big technology firms. Negative cash-flow reports from Alphabet and Tesla last week sparked a bout of selling in AI-linked stocks, with chip stocks also under pressure as investors questioned high valuations.
Meta Platforms tumbled after the social media heavyweight reported a 91 per cent drop in second-quarter free cash flow, indicating the financial strain of its costly AI buildout.
"These are true battleground stocks. Investors can't make up their minds whether the ROI on the massive capex spending is going to be worthwhile or not," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management.
"Microsoft delivered yesterday, and maybe Microsoft is going to be able to move itself from the 'battleground' camp to be a 'trusted AI winner' stock," Ellerbroek said.
The PHLX chip index surged 8.20 per cent, with Micron Technology jumping 18 per cent, Sandisk soaring 26 per cent and Advanced Micro Devices up 13 per cent.
Amazon rose 3.90 per cent and Apple dipped 1.40 per cent, with both companies set to report their results after the market closes.
Amazon's stock has underperformed the broader market this year due to concerns about heavy spending on AI.
Apple, which has not spent heavily on AI, recently overtook Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company, with a market value of about US$4.9 trillion.
The S&P 500 climbed 1.66 per cent to end the session at 7,437.63 points.
The Nasdaq gained 2.78 per cent to 25,122.18 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.19 per cent to 52,208.06 points.
Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by technology, up 5.20 per cent, followed by a 1.60 per cent gain in consumer discretionary.
On Wednesday, US stocks closed sharply lower after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, with mixed messages from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh leaving traders confused about the path of borrowing costs.
Bond markets remained on edge, with the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond surging to its highest level in 19 years.
Traders are now only pricing in a 59 per cent chance for a rate hike at the Fed's September meeting, according to CME FedWatch, down from 82 per cent a week ago.
US economic growth slowed in the second quarter as the trade deficit widened.
The economy grew at a 1.50 per cent rate, slower than estimates of 2.10 per cent growth, data showed. A separate reading also showed US inflation slowed in June.
Qualcomm fell 2.60 per cent after the chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected.
Fair Isaac slumped 17 per cent. Even though the credit-scoring giant lifted its annual profit and revenue forecasts, they remained below analysts' estimates.
Starbucks rose 1.60 per cent after the world's largest coffee chain raised its annual sales and profit forecasts.
Analysts on average expect S&P 500 aggregate second-quarter earnings to jump 40 per cent from a year ago, with AI-related stocks accounting for much of that growth, according to LSEG I/B/E/S.
Strong earnings forecasts and a recent decline in share prices have left the S&P 500 trading at about 20 times expected earnings, just above its 10-year average of 19, according to LSEG data.
Across the US stock market, advancing stocks outnumbered falling ones by a 2.2-to-one ratio.
Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 18.0 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.2 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

Title: Maybank: A new home for a six-decade institution [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: After more than six decades at the heart of the capital's old financial district, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is turning the page on its history.
The country's biggest bank has moved its headquarters into the landmark Menara Merdeka Maybank as it positions itself for the next chapter of growth.
The move brings the group's corporate functions under one roof at the 118-storey tower, signalling a new era for an institution that has grown alongside the nation since 1960.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim officiated the launch on Thursday, with Maybank chairman Tan Sri Ir Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa and president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli among those attending.
Ministers, senior government officials, regulators, board members, business leaders, clients and employees also witnessed the milestone.
For Anwar, the new headquarters represents more than a change of address.
He described the tower as a symbol of Malaysia's progress and a landmark of national pride, while congratulating Maybank's current and former leadership and employees whose contributions have shaped the institution over decades.
"Having served as Finance Minister for the past three to four years, I am grateful that Maybank has remained strong, not only in terms of financial success, but also in governance and the quality of its service.
"The challenge for Maybank is to continue safeguarding not only its financial performance but also its integrity.
"The institution's reputation is respected not merely because of its financial achievements, but because of the professionalism and integrity that underpin everything it does," he said.
A Move With Meaning
Zamzamzairani said the relocation symbolised Maybank's confidence in its future, anchored by its longstanding values and commitment to sustainable value creation.
"Since its establishment in 1960, Maybank has grown alongside Malaysia's development.
"Through various changes and challenges, we have remained steadfast in upholding the values of integrity, excellence and trust, which have formed the foundation of this institution's strength," he said.
As Malaysia approaches its National Day celebrations, Zamzamzairani said the occasion was a reminder that progress rests on strong foundations, trust and the determination to move forward.
Those same principles, he said, have guided Maybank for more than six decades and will continue shaping its future.
For Khairussaleh, the new headquarters is also a physical expression of the bank's ambitions under its ROAR30 strategy.
He said Maybank would continue focusing on a simpler, more seamless and personalised customer experience by combining its people, digital capabilities and regional network.
"We are equally committed to impacting society positively by expanding financial inclusion, empowering individuals and businesses through responsible and values-based financial solutions, while advancing education, strengthening communities and supporting environmental stewardship through our social impact initiatives.
"At the same time, we will continue to power the real economy by mobilising capital, facilitating trade and investment, and supporting businesses of all sizes to innovate, grow and thrive," he said.
The relocation formally closes one chapter while opening another.
On Tuesday, the Menara Merdeka 118 was officially renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, reflecting the bank's presence in the landmark tower.
Maybank occupies 33 floors of the building, which will accommodate about 7,000 employees.
The new headquarters will also house selected subsidiaries, including Maybank Islamic Bhd and Maybank Investment Bank Bhd.
Meanwhile, the bank's former headquarters on Jalan Tun Perak - long known as Menara Maybank - has been renamed Menara Tun Perak, with the change taking effect on July 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa raises IPO target to RM34bil as Q2 earnings jump 26pct [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd, which posted a 25.9 per cent increase in second-quarter earnings, has raised its initial public offering (IPO) market capitalisation target for 2026 to RM34 billion, backed by a robust listing pipeline.
Net profit for the quarter ended June 30 increased to RM71.78 million from RM57.06 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 22.3 per cent to RM210.97 million from RM172.58 million.
For the first half of 2026, net profit increased 15.2 per cent to RM144.61 million from RM125.48 million in the corresponding period last year, while revenue grew 19.1 per cent to RM425.04 million from RM356.78 million.
Operating revenue rose 19.6 per cent year-on-year to RM411.7 million, driven mainly by stronger securities trading activity, while operating expenses increased 21 per cent to RM229 million, mainly due to higher staff costs and regulatory fees.
Average daily trading value in the securities market rose 35 per cent year-on-year to RM3.3 billion, while average daily derivatives contracts increased 9.9 per cent to 106,518, driven mainly by crude palm oil futures.
The board declared an interim dividend of 16.5 sen per share amounting to about RM133.5 million, representing a dividend payout ratio of 92 per cent.
Chief executive officer Datuk Fad'l Mohamed said Bursa Malaysia had raised its IPO market capitalisation target for this year by RM6 billion from the original RM28 billion after surpassing it in the first half.
The exchange recorded 36 IPOs across the Main, ACE and LEAP markets during the six-month period, raising RM5.4 billion and contributing RM26.1 billion in market capitalisation, making Bursa Malaysia the leading Asean exchange by both IPO numbers and funds raised.
Fad'l said Bursa Malaysia expects one or two large IPOs in the second half of the year, supported by an encouraging pipeline across large-cap, mid-cap and ACE Market companies.
However, he said strong IPO activity does not necessarily translate into immediate improvements in the secondary market as the two are driven by different factors.
"IPO activities are driven by different sets of factors, including the quality of issuers, companies requiring capital to grow their businesses, and the strength of the IPO pipeline.
"Secondary market performance is exposed to different movements, including yields, the US dollar, foreign fund flows and broader risk management considerations," he said.
Fad'l said Bursa Malaysia would continue focusing on attracting quality companies and strengthening investor confidence through initiatives such as MyValueUp.
The programme aims to help listed companies articulate their long-term value creation plans, communicate them clearly to investors and support better valuation discovery.
He said the programme has received strong voluntary participation from listed companies, while institutional investors are also paying greater attention to companies with re-rating potential.
On the equity market, Fad'l said Bursa Malaysia supports a proposal to expand the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents to better reflect the breadth of the domestic equity market.
The proposal, issued jointly by Bursa Malaysia and global index provider FTSE Russell for market consultation, forms part of a broader review of the methodology for the FBM KLCI and the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid 70 Index (FBM70).
Currently, the 30 FBM KLCI constituents account for about 59 per cent of the Main Market's total market capitalisation. Expanding the benchmark to 50 constituents would increase coverage to around 70 per cent.
"The main objective of this proposal is to enhance sector representation and reduce concentration risks in certain sectors, particularly financial services," he said.
The financial services sector currently accounts for about 43 per cent of the FBM KLCI.
Under the proposal, its weighting is expected to decline to the mid-30 per cent range, allowing greater representation from sectors such as technology, energy and real estate investment trusts.
Separately, Fad'l said foreign investors returned to Malaysian equities in July as global market rotations continued following a correction in regional technology stocks.
Malaysia recorded positive foreign inflows during the month, with investors returning to sectors such as banking and utilities, which offer stable dividend yields.
"Markets continue to be rotational. Recently, we saw very high activities and flows into markets such as Taiwan and South Korea, driven by technology-related stocks and technology-related growth.
"As we have seen some correction in technology-related stocks, we are now seeing flows coming back to Malaysia," he said.
He said Malaysia continues to provide diversification opportunities for investors, supported by a balanced market participation base comprising retail investors, domestic institutions and foreign institutions.

Title: Milei demands expulsion of foreigners expressing 'hate' against Argentina
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: Argentine President Javier Milei on Thursday imposed a bar on foreigners who express "hate" towards the Latin American country, which he claims is the target of a sinister campaign.
Experts have cast doubt on the legal feasibility of the emergency decree, which is already in force but requires parliamentary approval to remain law.
The measure bars or expels foreigners deemed to have "spread or incited hate messages" against the country or its people.
In a statement, Milei said the measure was in response to "recent displays of hostility against the Argentine Republic and Argentines".
The ultraliberal leader appeared to be referring to public reactions to Argentina's recent World Cup final loss against Spain.
The decree follows his claims on Sunday that leftist administrations elsewhere in the Americas were leading an "anti-Argentine campaign".
It states that it does not impinge on constitutionally protected rights to express political, academic or ideological disagreements.
The measure generated immediate backlash from opposition parties.
Leonel Chiarella, president of the centrist Radical Civic Union party, said in a post on X that "the president's decree is unconstitutional" and argued that Argentina's Congress "should expressly reject it".
Opposition lawmaker Agustin Rossi said on X that the decree "mimics the anti-immigration logic of (US President Donald) Trump".
A legislative committee will review the urgency of the measure, which will then be examined by both deputies and senators and will only be thrown out if rejected by both chambers.
Lucia Galoppo, an international law specialist at the Center for Legal and Social Studies (CELS), said the measure "leaves too many grey areas".
"It does not specify what constitutes hate speech, how it will be defined, on what criteria, or how those who produce such speech will be identified," she told AFP.
COUNTRY OF IMMIGRANTS
It also runs counter to a long history of immigration in Argentina, which has one of the world's most lenient constitutions in this regard, according to sociologist Ivan Schuliaquer.
"Argentine history is very rich in the sense of being a country that has historically received immigrants from everywhere," he told AFP.
"We are not anti-immigrant," said Schuliaquer, who believes Milei "is taking advantage of a climate in society to capitalise on something that, generally speaking, has not been part of his political project".
The president appears to be hurting over Argentina's World Cup loss and events that followed the football final.
On Sunday, he lashed out at Brazil, Mexico and the US Democratic Party over what he claimed was an "anti-Argentine campaign" – apparently in reference to widespread criticism of the national team's performance in the last match.
Global football body FIFA is investigating the behaviour of several Argentina players in the loss, including alleged assault and unsporting behaviour.
FIFA will also investigate an incident following Argentina's 2-1 semi-final victory over England in which players held up a banner that read: "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" (The Falklands are Argentine).

Title: BN-PN 'alliance' faces litmus test
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan voters will head to the polls tomorrow to decide who governs the state for the next five years, but the outcome could have ramifications beyond its borders.
Beyond deciding the composition of the 36-seat state assembly, the election will test whether Barisan Nasional's electoral understanding with the Pas-led Perikatan Nasional can deliver results.
BN, which dominated Malaysian politics for more than six decades, entered the polls with an understanding with PN despite being the second-largest partner in Pakatan Harapan's unity government at the federal level.
PH is contesting all 36 seats, while BN and PN have avoided three-cornered fights by dividing the constituencies between themselves, with BN fielding candidates in 25 seats and PN in the remaining 11.
Bersatu, sidelined by PN, is contesting 24 seats on its own, although some analysts have questioned whether Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's party can significantly split the vote.
For BN and PN, the understanding effectively removes the vote-splitting between Umno and Pas that characterised previous elections, allowing both parties to concentrate their resources on challenging PH.
Whether that strategy succeeds will be one of the election's biggest political storylines.
Former Bangi member of parliament Dr Ong Kian Ming projected BN and PN could win 23 to 25 of the 36 seats, enough to form the next state government.
PH, however, has brushed aside such projections. Its communications director, Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, said political studies and speculation ultimately counted for little because elections were decided by voters.
That reflects the uncertainty surrounding a contest in which several plausible outcomes remain within reach.
In a scenario favouring BN, its grassroots machinery delivers despite contesting fewer seats, while enough moderate voters conclude that stability outweighs concerns over its understanding with PN.
Another favours PH, where it retains Chinese and Indian support while convincing enough Malay voters of the importance of continuity.
PH's caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has repeatedly framed the election as a referendum on his administration's performance.
Infrastructure and economic achievements may carry weight, but voters are also likely to ask whether those accomplishments have translated into tangible improvements to their daily lives.
The cost of living, employment opportunities, housing affordability and local development have consistently emerged as the issues that matter most on the campaign trail.
[[nid:1500873]]
Turnout may prove just as important. The Election Commission expects 72 to 75 per cent of voters to cast their ballots, citing the intensity of campaigning across the state.
About 225,000 of Negri Sembilan's 889,490 registered voters are aged under 30, and analysts believe they could emerge as kingmakers if turnout exceeds expectations.
Interviews from the ground suggest many younger voters are looking beyond jobs. They want stronger local economies, better opportunities and communities where they can build long-term futures instead of feeling that they have to leave their hometowns.
Sharp exchanges over development and governance have also marked the campaign.
[[nid:1500872]]
Former menteri besar Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan argued development had stalled after BN lost power in 2018.
Popularly known as Tok Mat, he said PH's two terms in office had amounted to little more than ribbon-cutting ceremonies with no meaningful changes on the ground.
Aminuddin, or Tok Min, defended the "ribbons" he had cut, saying they represented investments, industrial growth and employment opportunities rather than merely the opening of community halls.
By the time the final ballots are counted, Negri Sembilan voters will have decided far more than who governs the state for the next five years.
They will also have delivered an early verdict on whether BN's electoral understanding with PN can work, whether PH's alliance with BN at the federal level can last, and how Malaysia's increasingly fluid political alliances may shape the country's future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump announces agreement on disarmament of Hamas, Israeli withdrawal from Gaza
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that an agreement had been reached for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza, with Israeli forces set to withdraw as the process moves forward, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
Trump said the deal, which he described as a "historic" step towards peace and security, would be carried out in phases.
"The agreement will be carried out in carefully structured phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw, and the International Stabilisation Force will work with a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza being safe for its residents and its neighbours," he wrote in a post on his social media platform Truth Social.
He said the agreement represented a "major milestone" in implementing his 20-point plan for Gaza, adding that the territory would eventually be governed by a "new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people".
Trump also thanked Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye for their mediation efforts, saying their work, along with his administration's team, helped make the "historic breakthrough" possible.

Title: Brazilian Supreme Court justice authorises investigation into president's son
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca has authorised federal police to investigate Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, son of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, over suspicions he improperly helped a lobbyist in dealings with the health ministry, two sources with direct knowledge of the decision told Reuters.
Last week, federal police sought permission to open an investigation into Fabio Luis, known as "Lulinha", for alleged influence peddling and corruption on behalf of Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes in dealings with the ministry.
One line of inquiry is investigating whether Lulinha helped provide Antunes' businesses with access to health ministry officials in connection with a government deal involving a cannabidiol-based medication, one of the sources said.
Lawyers for Fabio Luis did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Antunes' legal representatives could not immediately be reached for comment.
The investigation into Fabio Luis has not yet been formally opened, a federal police source said.
Mendonca also granted federal police permission to launch another investigation into Lulinha earlier this year over allegations he received improper payments linked to a scheme involving irregular deductions from pensions administered by Brazil's National Social Security Institute (INSS), which also involved Antunes.
Asked about his son in a February interview with news outlet UOL, Lula said he had confronted Fabio Luis about the INSS case.
"If you've done something wrong, you'll pay the price for it. If you haven't, defend yourself," Lula told UOL.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'RCI shows govt's resolve in restoring trust in Tabung Haji' [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji has uncovered governance lapses and underscored the government's resolve to restore institutional integrity and accountability.
Putra Business School eco-nomist Professor Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said the findings reflected the government's willingness to confront past failures, hold institutions to account and strengthen safeguards against future misconduct.
"The RCI reveals the governance weaknesses affecting TH during a particular period of time.
"But most importantly we need to appreciate the fact that the government has taken the right approach in investigating what went wrong and ensuring such misconduct won't happen again," he said.
[[nid:1500943]]
On the potential impact on public confidence, Razman said depositor trust would depend on whether governance reforms continued to be implemented effectively.
"It will affect public confidence in Tabung Haji if there is no improvement on the governance aspect of it.
"However, based on what happened in the past three years, Tabung Haji has implemented the majority of the recommendations by the RCI.
"We have seen that the depositors remain loyal to Tabung Haji by not withdrawing their deposits but instead increasing them. The total deposits have already reached RM95 billion."
He said the steady growth in deposits suggested that reforms introduced in recent years had helped sustain public confidence in the pilgrimage fund despite the issues highlighted by the inquiry.
Razman added that continued improvements in governance and accountability would be essential to maintaining public trust and reinforcing confidence in Malaysia's institutional governance standards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm after clashes between Hindu and Muslim groups in the country's south sparked unrest that has left three people dead.
Shah, who has kept a low profile since being elected in March, broke his silence to deliver his first address to the nation, calling on his countrymen to be "responsible citizens and remove the clouds of unrest".
The violence began late Sunday in a village in the southern Sunsari district, which borders India, after an argument over loud music and the use of religious flags during a Hindu procession, according to officials.
Police opened fire to disperse the crowd, said local official Poshan Lamichhane. Two men died in the unrest, according to police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.
Authorities are investigating the deaths and have imposed a curfew in Sunsari and neighbouring districts to prevent further clashes.
A third man was killed on Thursday in the nearby Siraha district during a demonstration that took place while the curfew was in force.
"I, on behalf of the government, sincerely appeal to the citizens, civil society, religious communities, all respected leaders, all political parties and responsible media, to exercise patience and restraint and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity," Shah said in a video address.
Nepal, a secular republic where more than 80 per cent of the population is Hindu, has seen tensions flare occasionally in the southern plains, where sizeable Hindu and Muslim communities live side by side.
In his address, Shah vowed that the investigation would be "completely fair and transparent".
"The government is committed to bringing to justice whoever is responsible for the incident," he said.
Kafle, the police official, said efforts were being made to restore order.
"We have kept all police officials in the field on alert and are trying to protect public property and prevent any conflicting situation with minimal use of force," he told AFP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Blast at Pakistan coal mine complex kills at least 11, dozens missing
Article:
QUETTA: At least 11 coal miners were killed and dozens are missing after an explosion buried parts of a mining complex in Pakistan's Balochistan province on Thursday, an official said.
Shoaib Nosherwani, Balochistan's minister for mines and mineral development, told Reuters that 36 people were in the collapsed part of the complex at the time of the explosion.
Of them, 25 were missing late on Thursday night, he said.
Rescue efforts were under way at a depth of 4,000 feet (1,219 metres), said Muhammad Atif, the chief inspector of mines in the province.
"We are hopeful of finding some miners alive, but the chances are low," he said.
Abdul Ghani Baloch, a senior government mining official in the region, said: "Two mines close to each other were damaged in a powerful methane gas explosion."
The explosion occurred in Sorange, a remote area near the provincial capital, Quetta.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saudi sets up maritime defence alliance to secure Red Sea
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia said on Thursday it had set up a maritime defence alliance to secure navigation around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The move comes after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said last week they were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, and claimed attacks targeting Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and oil infrastructure in the kingdom.
The narrow maritime artery has been a critical waterway for delivering vast quantities of Saudi crude to the international market, after energy exports from the Gulf were largely choked off by the US-Iranian standoff in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Saudi defence ministry issued a joint statement on behalf of the 14 countries in the alliance: Bahrain, Bangladesh, Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Kuwait, Nigeria, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Turkiye and Yemen.
The ministry said the alliance was "aimed at enhancing maritime security, safeguarding freedom of navigation, securing international trade routes and energy supply lines, and protecting shared maritime interests in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden."
The ministry said it had invited 51 countries and organisations to a meeting about the alliance in Riyadh on Thursday.
It said representatives of 43 countries and an EU delegation attended, of which 14 countries confirmed their support while others were in the process of doing so.
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fire earlier this month for the first time in years, threatening a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mediator Pakistan says US-Iran talks ongoing as foes trade attacks
Article:
TEHERAN: Mediator Pakistan insisted on Thursday that negotiations between Iran and the United States were ongoing, even as Washington carried out a "heavy wave of strikes" on its foe in retaliation for fresh attacks targeting Jordan.
The last two days have seen Saudi Arabia join the US in striking fighter groups in Iraq, while Egypt has come under fire for the first time with a drone attack on a Mediterranean port, leading its president to warn that the Middle East conflict is facing a serious escalation.
On Thursday, Jordan reported intercepting Iranian missiles for a second day running, while Kuwait said an Iranian strike that hit a building belonging to a Chinese company killed one person.
The return to direct hostilities followed a brief pause in fighting meant to give talks a boost.
"Negotiations between parties are ongoing, particularly on (the) Strait of Hormuz and to de-escalate," Pakistani foreign ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi told reporters.
Pakistan had helped broker a deal between the warring sides laying the groundwork for negotiations on a permanent resolution, and Andrabi said it was doing its "utmost to bring all parties back" to technical talks under the agreement.
Previous talks following an April truce stalled, with the ceasefire collapsing earlier this month and Iran again slamming shut the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for oil and gas.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two oil tankers attempting to transit the strait with US support turned back after one of them caught fire.
Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, said it had set up a maritime defence alliance of 14 regional countries to secure navigation around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The move comes after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said last week they were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia and claimed attacks targeting Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea.
The narrow maritime artery has been a critical waterway for delivering vast quantities of Saudi crude to the international market after energy exports were choked off by the US-Iran standoff in the Strait of Hormuz.
[[nid:1500847]]
STRIKES IN IRAN
Earlier, the US military said it had "successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran", hitting dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets, including military command centres.
US President Donald Trump had vowed to hit Iran "hard" after Teheran's previous attack on Jordan, its first in the region in days.
The Guards' branch in the northwestern province of Zanjan said three of its members were killed in a US attack there.
Iran's state news agency IRNA also reported strikes on several cities in the southwestern Khuzestan province, as well as on Qeshm Island in the Gulf.
Areas around the cities of Abadan, Shadegan, Arvandkenar and Ahvaz – all in Khuzestan – were struck, the agency said, citing provincial authorities.
Jordan's army reported a new volley of Iranian missiles on Thursday morning, saying five had been shot down, causing no casualties.
The Guards confirmed the attack, saying the US "used the occupied bases in your country (Jordan) to launch an airstrike" that killed residents on Qeshm.
Kuwait's defence ministry denounced a "heinous" Iranian attack that "targeted a building belonging to a Chinese company in the north", killed one worker and caused severe material damage.
EGYPT HIT
Since it began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, the Middle East war has touched every country in the region, and some outside it.
While energy facilities elsewhere in the region have been repeatedly targeted by drones and missiles, Egypt had been spared until Wednesday, when an attack on a gas import hub sparked a fire that damaged two ships.
The government confirmed on Thursday that a drone was to blame for the blaze, noting that no one had claimed responsibility.
Yemen's Houthi rebels denied any involvement, according to rebel media.
In a post on X, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Egypt was "an important friend and partner" and suggested the drone attack was an Israeli false-flag operation.
Egypt's government said an inquiry was ongoing "to determine the circumstances of the incident and to take the necessary measures to preserve Egypt's interests and national security".
During a call to Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, Egypt's President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi stressed the need for "the international community to work together to halt this escalation", according to his spokesman.
Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler identified the damaged ships as the Energos Winter storage and regasification vessel and the GasLog Salem tanker, saying they had been moved offshore after the incident.
A private security monitor, UK-based Ambrey, reported that the US-owned and operated floating storage vessel had been hit by at least one drone.
The authority that manages the port said it remained fully operational.

Title: US Treasury anti-money laundering chief Gacki to join Citi as global head of sanctions
Article:
UNITED STATES: The US Treasury on Thursday said the director of its anti-money laundering Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Andrea Gacki, was stepping down to join Citigroup as the bank's global head of sanctions.
Gacki is leaving government service after 25 years at the Treasury and the Department of Justice and will remain at FinCEN for several weeks to support a smooth leadership transition, the Treasury said. She has headed FinCEN since 2023.
The department appointed career Treasury official and former FBI forensic accountant Jenna Casanova as acting FinCEN director.
Casanova most recently served as senior adviser to the Treasury undersecretary for terrorism and financial intelligence, where she worked on efforts to combat illicit finance and coordinated policies across FinCEN, the Office of Foreign Assets Control and other Treasury offices.
The Treasury said Casanova previously worked on FinCEN enforcement actions, helping lead the case that resulted in a record US$1.3 billion Treasury fine against TD Bank. That was part of US$3 billion in total penalties assessed for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act, the main federal anti-money laundering law.
Citi said Gacki will start on October 1 and join its Independent Compliance Risk Management leadership team, helping clients "navigate the increasingly complex sanctions landscape".
Brent McIntosh, Citi's chief legal officer and corporate secretary, who served alongside Gacki as Treasury undersecretary for international affairs during the first Trump administration, said Gacki was well respected in both the banking industry and government.
"Few leaders can match Andrea Gacki's depth of experience in sanctions and financial crime. Her history of thoughtful and proactive leadership makes all of us at Citi excited to have her joining as our Global Head of Sanctions," McIntosh said in a LinkedIn post.

Title: 'Use Adibah Amin's works in schools to foster unity'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
The works of acclaimed journalist, writer and educator Adibah Amin should be incorporated into the school curriculum to instil values of unity, tolerance and nationhood among younger generations, said former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali.
The Universiti Malaya pro-chancellor said Adibah's writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion and social cohesion.
"There is a seeming lack of understanding and tolerance of race and religion. If some agency can be moved to incorporate stories written by Adibah in schools, as part of the curriculum, it will go a long way towards planting the seeds of nationalism in the hearts and minds of our young people," she said at the "A Tribute to Adibah Amin: Book Reading" event at Monash University Malaysia here.
Zainun described Adibah's book 'As I Was Passing' as a precious collection whose significance would endure beyond the era in which it was written.
"Some stories are stories of the hour, while some are for all times. Adibah's 'As I Was Passing' belongs squarely to the latter," she said.
The tribute brought together figures from journalism, literature, education, the arts and civil society.
Adibah was unable to attend due to ill health.
A recipient of the Southeast Asian Writers Award, Adibah's "As I Was Passing" columns, written under the pen name Sri Delima and published in the 'New Straits Times' in the 1970s and 1980s, captured the humour, warmth and humanity of everyday Malaysian life.
Monash University Malaysia president and Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman said the university was pleased to celebrate Adibah's work alongside Malaysia's rich literary and cultural heritage.
Adeeba said the institution sought to embrace Malaysia's cultural diversity while celebrating the talents and achievements of Malaysians.
Organised by the Monash University Malaysia Library and Learning Commons, the programme featured readings of selected excerpts from the commemorative legacy edition of 'As I Was Passing: Glimpses of Malaysian Life' by five guest readers, alongside a video showcasing Adibah's life and contributions.
First compiled into a book in 2009, 'As I Was Passing' chronicles Adibah's observations of Malaysian society and continues to resonate in contemporary discussions on identity, community, and nationhood.
